messages.content: "Could you calculate the genetic similarity between a human and a chimpanzee, and then between a human and a gorilla, using their DNA sequences? Please provide the results in both percentage and fraction formats."

function.name: genetics_calculate_similarity
function.description: Calculates the genetic similarity between two species based on their DNA sequences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

format.description: The format of the result (percentage or fraction). Default is percentage.

We have a tool "genetics_calculate_similarity" which calculates genetic similarity between two species based on their DNA sequences. It takes arguments: species1, species2, format optional. We need to call this function twice: once with species1="human", species2="chimpanzee", format="percentage". Then again with same but format="fraction"? Or we can call it separately for each format. But the function signature expects format optional; default is percentage. So if we don't specify format, it returns percentage. If we set format="fraction", it returns fraction.

Thus we should call the function twice per pair: one for percentage, one for fraction. That means total four calls: human-chimp percentage, human-chimp fraction, human-gorilla percentage, human-gorilla fraction.

But maybe we can combine? The function only accepts one format at a time. So we need separate calls.

We need to output the results. We'll call the function accordingly.

We'll produce calls:

First call: species1="human", species2="chimpanzee", format="percentage".

Second call: species1="human", species2="chimpanzee", format="fraction".

Third call: species1="human", species2="gorilla", format="percentage".

Fourth call: species1="human", species2="gorilla", format="fraction".
